options: When you earn interest on both the money you save and the interest you earn
Earning interest only on the original deposit
Paying interest to a lender for borrowing
Withdrawing principal without earning interest
cards.quote: Compound interest: When you earn interest on both the money you save and the interest you earn.
cards.hint: Think about earning on both principal and prior interest

cards.stem: How is interest rate defined in the vocabulary list?
options: A percentage of a sum borrowed
A fee charged for closing an account early
A reward for withdrawing money quickly
A limit on monthly transactions
cards.quote: Interest rate: A percentage of a sum borrowed that is charged by a lender or merchant for letting you use its money.
cards.hint: Recall the definition that starts with a percentage term

cards.stem: Which action can help savings grow even faster?
options: Increasing the compounding frequency
Keeping money outside any account to avoid growth
Spending principal as soon as it is earned
Waiting longer to start saving for education
cards.quote: Increasing the compounding frequency or your interest rate or adding to your principal can help your savings grow even faster.
cards.hint: Consider what increases how often interest is added

cards.stem: What does the big idea say about timing of saving?
options: The sooner you start saving for post-secondary education
The later you start the faster money grows
Only scholarships can prepare for education costs
Saving has no effect on education expenses
cards.quote: The sooner you start saving for post-secondary education, the faster your money can grow from compound interest.
cards.hint: Remember the link between starting early and growth
